headline: Rent increases approved for 131 Sherman Street, 90 Pine Street, and 439 Congress Street; 117 Preble Street tabled.
summary: Approved rent increases for 131 Sherman Street, 90 Pine Street, and 439 Congress Street. Tabled the 117 Preble Street request until more cost details are received. Also approved new public access rules for rent board records and several findings.
decisions: Approved findings of fact and conclusions of law for 24 Row Avenue apartments one and two, 4-0.
Approved findings of fact and conclusions of law for Units 56 and 58 Federal Street, 4-0.
Approved findings of fact and conclusions of law for 341 Cumberland Ave, all 29 units, 4-0.
Removed $10,361 in legal expenses tied to a human rights commission matter from the 439 Congress Street costs, because the cost is not recurring, 4-0.
Approved the housing service cost increase application for 439 Congress Street, all 81 units, in the amount of $7.98, 4-0.
Found the 91 State Street application complete, pending more information on normal repairs, 4-0.
Approved changes to Article 11 of the rent board's rules of procedure on public access to records and applications, 4-0.
Tabled the 117 Preble Street rent increase application until more detailed information is received, 4-0.
Approved the rent increase application for 90 Pine Street, all four units, in the amount of $75.80, 4-0.
Found the $7,081.22 change in turnover expenses at 131 Sherman Street to be a capital improvement for unit six, to be amortized over five years and applied to unit six only, 4-0.
Struck $1,381.22 in 2022 legal fees from the 131 Sherman Street calculation as a one-time expense, 4-0.
Replaced the 2022 water and sewer cost at 131 Sherman Street with the 2021 cost increased by 3.7%, 4-0.
Approved the rent increase for 131 Sherman Street, with $50.69 for units one through five and $168.71 for unit six, 4-0.
Tentatively rescheduled the regular November meeting to November 18 at 5 p.m. Eastern time, 4-0.
discussion: 131 Sherman Street turnover costs: Members discussed whether costs to clean and repair one unit after an eviction should be treated as a one-time capital cost spread over several years, charged only to that unit.
131 Sherman Street objections: Tenants said most of the increase came from one unit's eviction and turnover, and they asked the board to deny the application.

117 Preble Street financial questions: Objectors questioned the age of the financial figures, the unit count, utility and insurance costs, and management fees, and the applicant was asked for more detail.
Article 11 public access rules: Members said the change keeps records public while limiting posting of applicant contact information, to reduce scam attacks on applicants.
Management fees at 131 Sherman Street: Tenants asked why management fees rose and said services declined, while the applicant said fees are set across its portfolio.
